context: Tests whether the agent picks the chat-history persistence layer (the right one for resuming conversations by user) rather than confusing it with generic agent persistence (crash recovery) or LongTermMemory (fact retrieval).

checklist.name: Installs ChatMemory with a PostgreSQL JDBC provider
checklist.description: Calls install(ChatMemory) and assigns chatHistoryProvider = PostgresJdbcChatHistoryProvider(dataSource), or an equivalent verified JDBC provider. Includes provider schema migration before serving requests. Does NOT install nonexistent JdbcChatHistory, Persistence (crash recovery), or LongTermMemory (fact retrieval).

checklist.name: Adds the JDBC chat-history dependency
checklist.description: Adds ai.koog:agents-features-chat-history-jdbc:1.3.0 and a PostgreSQL JDBC driver. Does not add chat-history-aws or agents-features-persistence-jdbc for this PostgreSQL conversation-resume request.

checklist.name: Reads DB credentials from environment
checklist.description: Reads DB_URL, DB_USER, DB_PASSWORD from System.getenv — none of the values are inlined. Also includes a Postgres JDBC driver in the dependencies (Koog does not bundle drivers)

checklist.name: Threads userId as sessionId on agent.run
checklist.description: Passes sessionId = userId (the developer's user identifier) on agent.run(...) calls. Does NOT generate a fresh UUID per request (would defeat the resume) and does NOT store sessionId inside the agent's storage (which is run-scoped, not session-scoped)

checklist.name: Does not require user to thread message history manually
checklist.description: Does not require the application code to load prior messages and prepend them to the prompt — the feature handles that. The route/handler just calls agent.run(input, sessionId = userId)
